Prerequisite(s): —

Benefit: A time mage can sometimes shorten an opposing spell's duration. A time mage can spend 2 motes of time as a standard action to attempt to decrease the duration of a spell or effect within 30 feet that has a duration of rounds per level. On a successful caster level check (1d20 + caster level) against a DC of 11 + the target spell's caster level, the duration of that spell or effect is decreased by a number of rounds equal to half the time mage's level, rounded down. If the duration is thereby reduced to zero or less, the spell ends immediately. The target spell's duration can only be shortened once in this way. Additional motes spent to further shorten the duration of a spell are wasted.
